findings.title: Base refusals lost when awk is dead: the B3 grep fallback cannot read a staged diff that holds a NUL, and does not run at all when awk passes the probe but fails on the file
findings.evidence: Hook lines (LF copy): 135-136 write the raw and textconv views with --text, so the raw bytes of any allowlisted image or font (with NULs) go into $STAGED_DIFF. Lines 167-169 are the one-line probe. Lines 209-216 are the fallback: it runs only when ADDED_LINES_AWK_OK is empty and reads with `grep -E '^\+' "$STAGED_DIFF"`. Measured base 845ece15 vs new, gitleaks stripped, rc as sh/dash: dead_awk_akia_after_png 1/1 -> 0/0; dead_awk_akia_after_ttf_assets 1/1 -> 0/0; dead_awk_pk_after_png 1/1 -> 0/0. In these three the awk shim exits 1, a docs/ or SmartCompareApp/assets/ PNG or TTF with valid magic is staged, and a later file holds an AKIA key or a PRIVATE KEY header. The control dead_awk_akia (no binary) stays 1/1 -> 1/1. Also file_dead_awk_akia 1/1 -> 0/0 and file_dead_awk_akia_with_env 1/1 -> 0/0: the awk shim passes the stdin probe but exits 2 on a file argument. In the second one a .env exists: the .env pass reads stdin, runs, and correctly finds no .env value. So the fix report's stated limit ('The .env value pass still refuses when a .env exists') is false. Mechanism measured: on a file with a NUL, GNU grep 3.0 prints 'Binary file X matches' instead of the lines; `tr -d '\000'` or `grep -a` restores them (grep >= 3.5 also suppresses the lines). The base hook's step 4 read the porcelain diff without --text, so an image never put a NUL into its stream. The base step-4 refusal is an existing check, and it is narrowed here.
findings.fix: Replace lines 209-216 with the old selection run UNCONDITIONALLY and NUL/locale-safe, the same patterns and messages, e.g. `if LC_ALL=C tr -d '\000' < "$STAGED_DIFF" | LC_ALL=C grep -E '^\+' | LC_ALL=C grep -Ev '^\+\+\+' | grep -qE '<four-branch ERE>'; then fail "<MSG_CREDENTIAL>"; fi` plus the same line with -e "$JWT_RE" -e "$CREDURL_RE" and the new-shapes message. The probe can stay. Cost: two greps. Add round-2 nodes (sh+dash): (1) dead awk + docs/a.png (valid PNG magic) + z.txt holding an AKIA key -> MSG_CREDENTIAL; (2) the same with a JWT -> MSG_NEW_SHAPES; (3) an awk that passes `printf '+x' | awk` but exits 2 when given a file -> MSG_CREDENTIAL. Then drop the wrong stated limit.

findings.title: CI secret-scan ERR backstop is fail-open on real gitleaks 8.30.1: a run that scanned nothing and found nothing passes the job
findings.evidence: ci.yml secret-scan step: the gitleaks call has no --no-color, then `grep -q ' ERR ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/gitleaks.log"`. I ran the step text taken from ci.yml (yaml.safe_load) under sh -e -o pipefail, with the REAL gitleaks 8.30.1 (Windows binary) behind a $RUNNER_TEMP/gitleaks wrapper. The case was a pull_request range whose head commit adds a runtime-built GitHub-token-shaped sentinel, plus a noisy-but-working textconv driver. Result: step rc=0. The log level is written as ESC[31mERR, the plain ' ERR ' is absent, and gitleaks reports 'no leaks found' after 'stderr is not empty'. The fix round measured the same fail-open with an invalid range (fix2/ci_err_probe.out). The node ci_gitleaks_err_line_fails uses a shim that prints plain text, so it cannot see this. In real CI a textconv cannot come from repo content, and the range-end check covers the main ERR source, so the practical reach is limited. The ruled backstop (TBF6/B2) is still ineffective.
findings.fix: Add --no-color to the CI gitleaks call (the `--exit-code 1 --ignore-gitleaks-allow --config ...` line), as the hook already does. Pin it by asserting '--no-color' in the CI shim argv in ci_gitleaks_err_line_fails, or with a static node. Not measured: that the Linux 8.30.1 binary also colours a file. That is inferred from the same logger.

findings.title: No node for an unreachable PR_BASE in the CI range-end check (mutant survives)
findings.evidence: ci_unreachable_range_end_fails_without_scanning (round-2 file, line 734) only tests a push whose 'before' is gone. The mutant ENDS="$PR_HEAD" (PR base not checked) leaves every CI node green. I reasoned this from the node source and did not execute it. With F2 open, an unreachable PR base makes git log fail, gitleaks logs a coloured ERR and exits 0, and the job passes silently.
findings.fix: Add ci_unreachable_pr_base_fails_without_scanning: EVENT_NAME=pull_request with a PR_BASE not in the clone -> rc != 0 and gitleaks calls == 0.

findings.title: Case-insensitive JPEG/TTF (and GIF/WEBP/OTF) extension rows are unpinned: deleting them is not detected
findings.evidence: Own mutants on LF byte copies: deleting `*.[Jj][Pp][Ee][Gg])` makes docs/Shot.JpEg (valid JPEG magic) refused (rc 1, expected 0). Deleting `*.[Tt][Tt][Ff])` makes SmartCompareApp/assets/fonts/X.TTF (valid magic) refused (rc 1, expected 0). A grep of tests/test_*precommit*.py finds no upper-case .JPEG/.TTF/.GIF/.WEBP/.OTF sample. a3_jpg_upper_case_extension_passes uses .JPG, and that only pins the [Jj][Pp][Gg] row.
findings.fix: Add pass nodes with valid magic for docs/x/IMG.JPEG, SmartCompareApp/assets/fonts/X.TTF and (optionally) .GIF/.WEBP/.OTF samples.

findings.title: git -c color.ui=always commit may defeat the hook's colour override for gitleaks (NOT MEASURED)
findings.evidence: Lines 478-480 force colour off through GIT_CONFIG_COUNT. In git's config.c, GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS (which `git -c ... commit` exports to the hook) is parsed after GIT_CONFIG_COUNT, so the user's -c value should win for gitleaks' own git diff. GREEN measured that gitleaks finds nothing under color.ui=always. My probe (probe3 git_c_color_ui_always, real gitleaks, GitHub-token shape) timed out at 180 s twice on the overloaded box. This only affects the gitleaks layer, not the six regex shapes.
findings.fix: Measure. If it is confirmed, append the override after the user's parameters for the gitleaks call: GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="${GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS:+$GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS }'color.ui'='never' 'color.diff'='never'".

findings.title: Under sh -x / dash -x the binary check traces 12 content bytes of every staged binary
findings.evidence: Line 276: `_head=$(git cat-file blob ":$_bin" | od -An -tx1 -N12 | tr -d ' \n')` is an assignment, so xtrace prints it with its value. For a disguised dump at an allowlisted path, those are the first 12 bytes of content, e.g. 12 of the 20 characters of a raw AKIA key, before the refusal. This is shell semantics and was not measured: the xtrace probe did not run. The .env values stay protected (4b disables xtrace).
findings.fix: Optional: wrap the binary loop in the same `{ set +x; } 2>/dev/null` and restore block that 4b uses.

findings.title: Temp dir now always holds the full staged diff; untrapped signals leave it behind
findings.evidence: make_tmp runs unconditionally (line 132): staged.diff, staged.ext and gitleaks.err are written for every commit, while the base hook made a temp dir only for staged .py or SKILL.md blobs. Measured: 0 leftovers in TMPDIR or .git after all 116 hook runs of the 29 scenarios (refusal and pass paths), and after every shim and real-gitleaks run. Not measured: QUIT, PIPE and KILL (only INT, TERM and HUP are trapped). The signals probe did not run. The dir is mode 700 (mktemp or umask 077).
findings.fix: None required. Optionally add QUIT and PIPE to the trap at line 36.

summary: DEFECTIVE: one finding breaks the additivity principle, and one is a fail-open CI backstop. (1) If awk is dead, steps 4 and 4a fall back to a grep over the staged-diff file. That grep reads nothing as soon as the file holds a NUL, and the --text views put a NUL there for any allowlisted PNG or TTF staged in the same commit. The fallback also never runs when awk passes the one-line probe but fails on the file. Measured base->new 1/1->0/0 (sh/dash) in five scenarios where the base hook refused an AKIA key or private-key header. The fix-round stated limit about the .env pass covering this is false. Smallest fix: always run the old grep selection, NUL- and locale-safe (LC_ALL=C tr -d '\\000' | grep). (2) The CI ERR check never trips on real gitleaks 8.30.1 output, because it lacks --no-color. Replaying the ci.yml step with the real binary passed a PR range that holds a GitHub-token shape (rc 0, coloured ERR, 'no leaks found'). The fix is one flag plus a pin. Also: no node covers an unreachable PR_BASE or the upper-case JPEG/TTF rows (mutants survive). The git -c color bypass of gitleaks is plausible but unmeasured. Clean: hostile work-tree .gitleaks.toml ignored; ERR/INF/WRN shim rules behave as ruled; honest session-72 docs checkpoint passes under the unit config; no sentinel was printed and no temp dir was left across 116+ hook runs. This box's slow-spawn pathology (node -e 0 up to 10 s) cut the additivity set to 29 of 71, and pytest killing nodes were not executed (mutants were replayed on byte copies).
